subject: general
question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Khilafat Movement**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Khilafat Movement was led by the Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali) and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**

 
 
• to protest against the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire after World War I and to protect the institution of the Caliphate,
 
 
• which they considered a symbol of unity among Muslims.
 
 
 
• It was a **significant movement in India,** seeking to rally Muslims and Hindus in opposition to British rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Wahabi Movement:
 
 
• It emerged in the early 19th century in India, inspired by the teachings of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab in Arabia.
 
• The movement aimed to purify Islam by removing practices considered to be innovations (bid'ah) and restoring monotheism (tawhid).
 
• It also opposed British colonial rule and encouraged jihad against foreign powers, becoming associated with resistance movements in India.
 
 
 
• Faraizi Movement:
 
 
• It was started by Haji Shariatullah in Bengal in the early 19th century, focusing on the strict observance of Islamic obligations (Faraiz).
 
• The movement sought to eliminate un-Islamic practices and customs that had crept into the lives of Bengali Muslims, particularly under British rule.
 
• It also had an anti-landlord and anti-colonial component, with a significant following among peasants, advocating for their rights against oppressive landlords.
 
 
 
• Ahmadiya Movement:
 
 
• Founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in 1889 in India, the movement claims that Ahmad is the promised Messiah and Mahdi of Islam.
 
• It promotes peaceful propagation of Islam and stresses rational discourse, interfaith harmony, and religious tolerance.
 
• The movement is controversial within mainstream Islam due to its belief in Ahmad’s prophetic role, which is seen by some as a challenge to the finality of Prophet Muhammad’s prophethood
